title: Hair.js
summary: Polygon script that grows hair/fur polygons (optionally along spline guides) on a child base mesh; later cHair.js variant adds hair count and random seed.

evidence.quote: I have just updated Hair.js script for 5.2 User. old one won't work

evidence.author: teamdallas

api_lessons: Do not name a script parameter "type": it collides with a hidden built-in parameter and the script object vanishes after save and reopen. Rename it (e.g. "hair type").
In 4.6, the value returned by PolyCore.uvCoord() could not be used directly with Vec2D methods; wrap it: uv = new Vec2D(uv.u, uv.v) before calling add().
Script folders map to menus: Tool, Splineobj, Polygonobj, Tag, Macro under ~/Library/Application Support/Cheetah3D/scripts/. Relaunch or use 'Update Scripts Menu' (5.x+) after installing.
Procedural scripts that use Math.random() give different results after save and reopen; add a random-seed parameter so results are reproducible.
A polygon script can output two UV sets: Hair.js puts the base mesh's UV1 into the hair's UV1 and the hair's own UVs in UV2, so material channels can choose either.
notes: Hosted only on tres-graficos.jp (id=44 general, id=52 for 5.2+, id=63 cHair.js). Hair.js needs Cheetah 3.5+. Hair.js gave a line 242 error in 6.2.1 while cHair.js worked. Hair does not follow morph/deformation animation of the base mesh (unresolved). Slow on dense meshes; use the 'modified child' option only before rendering. Newer macOS hides ~/Library, which confuses installation.

title: How to add animation keyframes?
summary: Q&A on creating keyframes from script; answer: impossible before v6, then tg_jp gives an F-curve tool script example.

evidence.author: crgreen
evidence.quote: no keyframes are set, even if I have automatic keying turned on

evidence.author: Martin
evidence.quote: I'm sorry but that never worked. v6 will be the first version which adds access to the animation data.

evidence.author: tg_jp
evidence.quote: here is a sample code of tool script to add animation f-curve for selected object.

api_lessons: Before Cheetah 6 there was no script access to animation data: doc.setAnimPosition() plus setParameter() does NOT create keyframes, even with auto-keying on (Martin). An earlier claim that this works is wrong.
Cheetah 6+ keyframing: param = obj.parameterWithName('scale'); node = param.takeNodeWithName(doc.currentTake().name) || param.addTakeNode(doc.currentTake().name); curve = node.fCurveAtIndex(i).
For Vec3D parameters, fCurveAtIndex(0/1/2) are the x/y/z component curves.

Build keys with new FCurveKey(): set time (in seconds, not frames), value, left_type/right_type (e.g. SPLINE_INTERPOL), and left_time/left_value/right_time/right_value (relative to the key). Then curve.addKey(key) and call curve.update(). curve.removeAllKeys() clears existing keys.
notes: versions_working '6' refers to the F-curve approach that Martin announced and tg_jp's sample demonstrates; the requester thanked but did not confirm running it.

api_lessons: (2008) There was no API to assign a material to an object; the scripts name the new objects after the material so you can assign it by hand.
The pre-5.0 approach doc.materialAtIndex(tag.linkedToMaterial()) broke after 5.0.
Post-5.0 workaround: loop obj.tagAtIndex(i), check tag.type() == 102 (material tag), and read the material through the link parameter: tag.getParameter("material").getParameter("name").
Combiner-2 identifies materials by name, not by id, so material names must be unique in the document.

api_lessons: To move a pivot without moving geometry: offset every vertex with core.setVertex(i, core.vertex(i).sub(c)), then obj.setParameter("position", obj.objMatrix().multiply(c)) and call obj.update().
Check that a core is a polygon core with typeof(core.polygonCount) == "function" before using polygon methods.
Area/centroid calculations that rely on Cheetah's internal triangulation (core.triangle) can fail on some non-convex n-gons.
Read the face selection with core.polygonSelection(i).
notes: Author states it requires C3D 5.0+ (versions_working reflects that, not a user report). The archived file is the 2009 forum version, which handles rotation and scale. The 2013 centre-of-volume version is only at loewald.com/c3dbook. Gives erratic pivots on flat (2D) objects.

title: Can't find variable: SPOTLIGHT
summary: Martin's bundled 'Scale Light Intensity' tool script fails in 5.3 because the light-type constants were removed; a corrected script is posted.

evidence.quote: error: Can't find variable: SPOTLIGHT

evidence.author: tg_jp
evidence.quote: the constants SPOTLIGHT, DISTANTLIGHT, and AREALIGHT seems to be gone.

evidence.author: Nichod
evidence.quote: Corrected script:

api_lessons: Since 5.x, all lights are a single object type, LIGHT. The constants POINTLIGHT/SPOTLIGHT/AREALIGHT/DISTANTLIGHT are undefined and cause 'Can't find variable'. Test obj.type() == LIGHT instead. (The 8.1.1 reference Constants page still lists them and does not list LIGHT, so check before relying on either.)
The light subtype is the Int parameter "lightType" (spot light = 4). Brightness is "intensity". Other light parameters include color (Vec4D), cutOffAngle, shadowType, and photonLight.
Introspection: obj.parameterCount(), parameterAtIndex(i), and parameterInfo() reveal parameter names and types (podperson's Object Info script). Tag type ids seen: MODETAG = 103, PROPWINTAG = 104.
notes: Fix: replace the multi-constant test with objtype == LIGHT.
